name: Karasawa cirque and Okuhotaka (涸沢・奥穂高岳)
why: Up the Azusa valley into the great rock bowl of Karasawa, then on chains and ladders to the top of Japan's third highest mountain.
book: Book the huts ahead (Karasawa Hutte or Karasawa-goya, Hotakadake Sanso). No private cars to Kamikochi: bus from Sawando, Hirayu or Shin-Shimashima. Climbing from Kamikochi takes two nights; do not try it as a day hike.
water: Water at the huts of Tokusawa, Yokoo and Karasawa; at Hotakadake Sanso it is sold. The water at Hontani bridge is not safe to drink.
dangers: The Zaitengrat rock ridge above Karasawa and the summit block above Hotakadake Sanso have chains and ladders: a slip there is a fall. A helmet is advised.
Falls on the Hotaka ridges kill several climbers every year; in wind, rain or snow do not go above the hut.
Snow in the Karasawa bowl until July and from October: then crampons are needed.
Afternoon thunderstorms in summer: be at the hut by early afternoon.
turnaround: If the rock is wet or the cloud is down at Karasawa, stay there and enjoy the cirque: the Zaitengrat is not a place for bad weather.

points.name: Kamikochi bus terminal
points.note: 1,500 m. Over Kappa Bridge and up the flat valley past Myojin: about 2 hours to Tokusawa.

points.name: Tokusawa
points.note: A meadow with elms, a lodge and a campsite under the east face of Mae-Hotaka. Yokoo, where the path turns into the mountains, is 1 hour 10 minutes on.

points.name: Karasawa cirque
points.note: Night 1 at about 2,300 m, at Karasawa Hutte in a glacial bowl walled by the Hotaka peaks; famous for autumn colours in late September.

points.name: Hotakadake Sanso
points.note: Night 2 at about 2,980 m, on the col between Okuhotaka and Karasawadake, reached up the Zaitengrat ridge in about 3 hours.

points.name: Okuhotaka summit
points.note: 3,190 m, 50 minutes above the hut by ladders and chains. Yarigatake to the north, Mount Fuji far to the south-east. Back the same way.
